subject: Onramp surge readout & renewal recommendation (Q3 renewal)
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@orbitize.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onramp surge readout & renewal recommendation (Q3 renewal)

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the sync last week. Attached is a short readout of the onramp surge we saw in July and a recommended path for the upcoming renewal. Highlights: 

- Token spend increased ~2.6x during the feature preview (see Q3-usage-report.xlsx).
- Latency remained within SLO for 95th pct but CPU-backed degradation occurred during large batch jobs (see latency-sample-logs.txt).
- Current committed capacity will cover baseline, but not peak surges; without change you risk throttles next month.

Recommendation (quick):
1) Move to a 20% uplift on committed tier to cover expected growth windows.
2) Add a 50k burst-credit buffer for quarter 1 of the renewed term.
3) Enable the quantized model variant for inference paths where cost sensitivity is high — we estimate 18–22% unit-cost savings.

I've attached the raw usage and logs. If this looks reasonable, I can route a short amendment with pricing and a PO flow for procurement.

Next steps: can you confirm internal stakeholders and the preferred procurement timeline?

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Lead Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Q3-usage-report.xlsx, latency-sample-logs.txt

From: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@orbitize.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Kramer <ava.kramer@orbitize.com>, procurement@orbitize.com
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onramp surge readout & renewal recommendation (Q3 renewal)

Thanks Naomi — helpful breakdown. A couple quick clarifying questions before we loop procurement: 

- Can you confirm whether the 20% uplift assumes the quantized variant across all endpoints or just a subset? We saw some quality delta for the summary endpoint during the preview.
- What SLA do we get on burst-credit availability (i.e., is that guaranteed or best-effort)?

If you can provide a one-page econ summary we can present to our engineering and finance leads (Ava will own ops). We are targeting a decision by 8/10.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Onramp surge readout & renewal recommendation (Q3 renewal)

Naomi / team — quick internal note to line up the recommendation for Jordan's questions.

Summary of our view after looking at the logs and the usage model (commit-econ-model.xlsx attached):
- The 20% uplift assumes quantization on non-summary endpoints only (chat / semantic search can use quantized 8-bit; summary endpoint stays on float16 for fidelity). This keeps observed quality delta under 1.5% for summary BLEU-like metrics while saving ~20% on token cost for other paths.
- Burst credits are a negotiated bucket; we recommend a contract clause that guarantees immediate allocation up to the purchased burst pool and an autopruning policy if sustained usage exceeds the buffer for >24 hours.
- Financial impact: moving to the uplift + burst buffer with partial quantization is net neutral in month-1 against their forecasted spend because savings from quantization offset commit delta; month-2+ shows ~12% efficiency on tokens.

Recommended customer-facing language (short):
"We recommend a 20% committed uplift and a 50k burst-credit buffer for Q1. We'll enable quantized model variants on non-summary endpoints to preserve summary quality while reducing unit cost; we estimate a 12% net token cost reduction by month two."

If Naomi is comfortable, I'll draft the amendment and the pricing table — Ben, Monica: any constraints from billing or legal on the burst clause?

-Karthik
Director, Revenue Strategy

Attachments: commit-econ-model.xlsx

From: Procurement Team <procurement@orbitize.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Naomi/Karthik — thanks for the clear recommendation. Procurement has reviewed the econ model and the proposed burst language; we're happy to proceed with the following steps: 

1) Orbitize to sign the renewal amendment with the 20% uplift and 50k burst credits.
2) Procurement will issue a PO once we receive the amendment + final pricing table and the redlined burst policy. Target PO delivery: 2027-08-12.
3) Please provide a one-page scoping doc for our legal team that summarizes the quantization carve-outs (which endpoints, rollback policy, and quality guardrails).

Attached: draft_PO_orbitize.pdf (placeholder PO template).
